extracted.intended_audience: editors, reviewers, and authors participating in software/package peer review (rOpenSci community and similar projects)
extracted.subtask_description: Practices and procedural standards for managing peer review of software packages: scope screening, recruiting reviewers, handling dropouts, workload management, automation, and onboarding editors. Focused on the rOpenSci package review context but applicable to other software-review efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: After a package is submitted, the rotating Editor-in-Chief has to assess whether it is in scope for the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Traditionally rOpenSci’s scope has focused on packages that manage the research data lifecycle to form a coherent set of tools and to limit packages to those editors/reviewers can review with relevant standards and expertise. Scope descriptions should be refined over time to handle edge cases; better phrasing and examples help authors evaluate scope before submission. The scope is expanding to include statistical packages and will be refined further.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission inquiry for scope clarification
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage package authors to submit a pre-submission inquiry before a full submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A pre-submission inquiry helps clear doubts about whether a package is in scope and can prevent inappropriate full submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consensus-based handling of ambiguous scope
rubrics_metrics.description: When the scope of a package is ambiguous, the Editor-in-Chief leads a discussion on the editorial Slack channel with other editors to come to a consensus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In these discussions editors acknowledge differing expertise and sometimes consult subject experts external to the board to gain more insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for choosing reviewers (diversity & workload management)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a list of criteria for choosing reviewers to ensure diversity in both skills and background, and to continuously build up a pool of experienced reviewers without overloading any of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect finer-grained data about technical and topical expertise and availability; ask optional demographic/underrepresentation question to support diversity. Maintain reviewer histories to avoid overloading and to match expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect detailed reviewer metadata (volunteer form & database)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a reviewer volunteering form to collect fine-grained data about technical and topical expertise and optional self-identification about underrepresented status; store this in a database with each reviewer’s history of reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain the database (Airtable) as a resource for editors to find reviewers with particular expertise, background, or availability; use it to manage reviewer workloads and recruitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear review request response expectation (one-week default)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add explicit language to review request templates: “If I don’t hear from you within a week, I will assume you are unable to review at this time.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This wording clarifies expectations for potential reviewers and helps editors know when to move on after waiting for a response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling reviewer dropouts and replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reviewer drops out (or can no longer be contacted), the handling editor recruits a replacement or the editor acts as a second reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often recruit someone who can provide a short turnaround (for example another editor). The goal is to not delay the review process too much.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set reviewer time expectations (reviews take similar time as papers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that reviewing a package takes precious time and is about the same time as reviewing a scientific paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a reviewer guide to make the experience easier and more valuable to reviewers; be mindful of reviewers' schedules when recruiting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preventing and managing authors dropping out
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors stopping responding requires stopping the review; to reduce simple communication problems, recommend authors enable GitHub notifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To address maintenance/commitment concerns, add author-guide/submission template language: “I expect to maintain this package for at least 2 years or to find a replacement.” For larger time/commitment problems, apply holding labels and revisit holds every three months, up to one year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use holding labels and periodic revisits for stalled reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply holding labels to put reviews on hold when needed and revisit these holds on a schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holds are revisited every three months, up to one year, to manage stalled reviews without losing track of them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automation to reduce editorial work (GitHub chatops and bot)
rubrics_metrics.description: Automate editorial tasks using a GitHub chat-bot that manages the editorial process: assigning tasks, tagging issues, running tests on submissions, returning reports to reviewers and editors, and logging reviews in an external database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of bot usage: '@ropensci-review-bot check package' to run checks; '@ropensci-review-bot add @maelle to reviewers' to register a reviewer. Automation reduces manual steps like cloning, installing dependencies, running checks, and posting results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor workload targets and staffing model
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit expected load per editor and expand editorial team to share work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for editors to handle about 4 submissions a year. Recruit new editors largely out of the pool of experienced reviewers, invite guest-editors, and ask editors for 2-year commitments (with option to renew).

rubrics_metrics.name: Onboarding and documentation for editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an editor guide to facilitate onboarding of new editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Onboarding leads to feedback and improvements to the guide; encouraging reviewers to volunteer is a pathway to become an editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage direct editor-to-editor communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Enable editors to communicate directly (e.g., Slack) to find solutions, commiserate, and encourage each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct communication helps in recruiting reviewers, resolving scope ambiguities, and sharing operational solutions—something editors valued compared to more siloed traditional journals.
